summary:
SPACEm9 — The CLPS Lunar Mission Browser is a native Android application engineered by Team !!!NASAxISRO!!! for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. This application serves as a mobile dashboard for tracking robotic missions under NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) framework. Built with Jetpack Compose and Kotlin, it resolves data fragmentation by pulling isolated orbital paths, mission manifests, and instrument profiles into a single offline-first repository. The app delivers a low-latency, responsive mobile UI optimized for space planners, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts.
Key application features include:
• Interactive Moon Map: A vector-rendered surface viewer built to inspect landing zones, coordinates, and local geography directly on your device.
• Mission Comparison Engine: A multi-column interface designed to cross-reference flight timelines, target orbits, and operational parameters side-by-side.
• Payload Deep Dive: Granular data grids breaking down the weight, power, and scientific objectives of tools carried by commercial landers.
• Mobile Trajectory Hub: A lightweight utility enabling users to filter telemetry datasets, calculate delta-v budgets, and verify launch windows.

The app can be downloaded on a Android Mobile device (supporting .apk files) using this link-
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Yr63-UxK_EJKUZRTe1zkQZ9Ux4h8Vv2f/view?usp=drivesdk
